lines.text: by riding the marathon in a car.
See, at the nineteen oh four Olympics, athletes ran the marathon on a dirt road in brutal heat,
and the race director refused to give them water,
so he could study what dehydration does to the body.
Cars kicked up clouds of dust. Runners cramped, collapsed, and quit.
One Cuban postman stopped mid-race to snack on rotten apples.
And a South African runner got chased a mile off course by a pack of wild dogs.
Meanwhile, the leader, Thomas Hicks, was begging for water.
So his trainers gave him something better.
Strychnine, rat poison, mixed with raw egg white and brandy.
He hallucinated, collapsed at the finish, and was carried over the line.
He still won gold, in three hours, twenty eight minutes,
still the slowest winning time in Olympic history.
Oh, and Fred Lorz? He said it was just a joke.
A year later, un-banned, he won the Boston Marathon, for real.
